draft.title: The Murray-Darling Basin Plan
card: The Murray-Darling Basin Plan is a national plan made law in 2012. It aims to share the basin's water in a way that keeps rivers healthy and supports people who use the water.
The Plan sets sustainable limits on how much water can be taken from the rivers each year, for irrigation, towns and industry.

Some water is returned to the rivers and wetlands to support plants, animals and river health. Governments do this partly by buying water entitlements from irrigators and partly by funding more efficient irrigation.

People disagree about the Plan. Some irrigators and towns worry that less water for farming costs jobs and income. Conservationists may argue that the rivers still need more water than the Plan returns.
draft.remember: The Plan caps water taken and returns some to the rivers, and people disagree over where the balance should sit.

a.q: What is the main purpose of environmental flows under the Basin Plan?
opts: To return water to the rivers and wetlands for their health
To deliver extra water to irrigators during dry years
To supply water to towns that are far from the river
To move water from the basin to coastal cities
a.why: Environmental flows are water set aside for the rivers and wetlands, so plants and animals can survive. Supplying irrigators is tempting, but that is water taken for use, not water returned to the rivers.
a.clue: Think about who the returned water is meant to help.

b.q: A town in the basin has lost some farm work since the Plan began. Why might its residents and conservationists disagree about the Plan?
opts: Residents fear lost jobs, while conservationists want river health
Residents want more dams, while conservationists want fewer farms
Residents oppose every limit, while conservationists oppose all use
Residents want the Plan scrapped, while conservationists want no change
b.why: Residents focus on the income and jobs that farm water supports, and conservationists focus on river health. The other options use words like every, all and scrapped, which claim more than the card says: groups hold a range of views, and conservationists may want more water returned, not no use at all.
b.clue: Each group is thinking about a different thing the water supports.

a.q: What is the main purpose of environmental flows under the Basin Plan?
opts: To keep rivers and wetlands healthy for plants and animals
To give irrigators extra water during dry years
To supply drinking water to towns in the basin
To carry water from the basin to coastal cities
a.why: Environmental flows are water put back into the rivers and wetlands so plants and animals can survive. Giving irrigators extra water is tempting, but that is water taken out for use, which the limits control.
a.clue: Is this water meant for people to use, or for the river system?

b.q: A town in the basin has lost some farm work since the Plan began. Why might its residents and conservationists disagree about the Plan?
opts: Residents worry about jobs, conservationists about rivers
Residents worry about rivers, conservationists about jobs
Residents worry about dams, conservationists about cities
Residents worry about rain, conservationists about farm jobs
b.why: Residents depend on the jobs and income that farm water supports, while conservationists argue the rivers need more water. The reversed option is tempting because it names the same two concerns, but it gives each group the other's worry.
b.clue: Which group depends on farm work for a living?
